resale_co.name: Construction Records Clearance (CRC)
resale_co.issued_by: Town of Clinton Construction Office (Construction & Zoning)
resale_co.lead_time: Submit far enough ahead of closing to allow review and any inspections; the fee rises if the application comes in within 10 business days of closing
requirements: Records review for open construction permits (office checks open permits before issuing the Certificate of Records Clearance)
Application asks whether there is a swimming pool and a pool barrier
Application asks whether a water heater, HVAC, woodstove or fireplace insert was installed or replaced
Application asks whether a deck, hot tub, shed or outbuilding, or finished basement was built
Application asks whether the smoke, carbon monoxide and fire extinguisher application has been filed

fees.label: Construction Records Clearance application, submitted within 10 business days of closing
fees.quote: Application Fee: $150.00 if submitted within 10 business days of closing

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the Construction Records Clearance Application from the Town's Municipal Forms page, fill it out and submit it with the fee to the Construction Office, 43/47 Leigh Street. Questions go to the Technical Assistant to the Construction Official at 908-735-2275.
resale_co.contact_title: Technical Assistant to the Construction Official

evidence.quote: Whenever any residential property is sold, the current owner must submit the following two applications and receive final approval from the Town before the sale can occur
It is recommended that the applications above be submitted far enough in advance of the scheduled closing to allow sufficient time to review and schedule the applicable inspections.
If you have any questions on either of the forms above, please contact Catherine Innella via email or at 908-735-2275.
Town of Clinton Construction Records Clearance Application
Records clearance fee: $150 (submitted within 10 days of closing).
Catherine Innella - Technical Assistant to the Construction Official

resale_co.notes: The Town's 'Selling your Residential Property' page says the owner must get final approval on two applications before any residential sale: the Construction Records Clearance and the smoke/CO/fire extinguisher certificate. No Town Code section requiring the CRC was found in the ecode360 chapters checked; the Fees chapter (73-3G(18)) lists the $150 late records clearance fee, and the regular $100 fee comes from the application form. The Town's fee chapter also lists a 'certificate of continued occupancy' fee of $200, but no page ties it to 1-2 family sales. The 'Selling' page links the contact name to the email awitt@clintonnj.gov, while the Construction & Zoning page and staff directory give cinnella@clintonnj.gov for Catherine Innella. The rental certificate of occupancy (Code Enforcement Housing Officer, $35) applies to rentals only. The packs.json ecode link CL0749 is the Town of Clinton code (correct for this town).

requirements: Smoke alarm on each level of the home and outside each separate sleeping area
Battery-only smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed battery units; hardwired alarms from original construction may not be replaced with battery alarms
Carbon monoxide alarm in the immediate vicinity of the sleeping areas (where there is a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage)
Portable ABC fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen along the exit path, no more than 10 pounds, mounted no higher than 5 feet, with a service tag within 1 year or new (form still lists it)

authorities.name: Town of Clinton Fire Safety & Prevention (Department of Fire Prevention, Fire Marshal)
authorities.lead_time: Submit the application 4 to 5 weeks before closing; the inspection is scheduled about 2 weeks before the closing date

fees.label: Smoke/CO/extinguisher certificate, application more than 10 business days before change of occupant
fees.quote: Application received more than 10 business days prior to a change of occupant: $45.00

fees.label: Application 4 to 10 business days before change of occupant
fees.quote: Application received 4 to 10 business days prior to a change of occupant: $90.00

fees.label: Application fewer than 4 business days before change of occupant
fees.quote: Application received fewer than 4 business days prior to a change of occupant: $161.00

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Town's 'Smoke-CO Alarm-Fire Extinguisher Application' and send it with a check or money order payable to the Town of Clinton. The owner may either ask the Department of Fire Prevention to inspect, or self-certify the alarms on the form with a notary's authentication if the Fire Official permits it.

evidence.quote: APPLICATION FOR ONE & TWO FAMILY DWELLING CERTIFICATE OF SMOKE ALARM AND CARBON MONOXIDE ALARM AND FIRE EXTINGUISHER COMPLIANCE
Please submit the application 4 to 5 weeks prior to the planned closing date.
*SMOKE DETECTOR/CARBON MONOXIDE CERTIFICATES ARE VALID FOR SIX (6) MONTHS*

The local Department of Fire Prevention may conduct this inspection however an owner, an authorized representative of the owner may be permitted to conduct this inspection provided a notary authenticates that inspection statements made upon this form are true.
A current unobstructed portable ABC type fire extinguisher is hung within 10 feet of the kitchen
The application fee for a certificate of smoke detector and carbon monoxide compliance shall be as established by the Uniform Fire Code.
Clinton Town1005 LEAID: 1005-001 Enf Auth. Municipal Fire Official John K Daniels Phone (908) 735-2275 Email jdaniels@clintonnj.gov

fire_cert.notes: The Town of Clinton enforces the fire code locally (LEA code M). The Town's application (revised 7-19-25) sets fees of $45.00 / $90.00 / $161.00, says certificates are valid for six months and are not transferable, and allows a notarized owner self-certification as an alternative to the Fire Prevention inspection. The form still lists a portable fire extinguisher, although P.L.2025, c.19 dropped it from the state sale certificate in February 2025; confirm with the office. Phone numbers differ: the Town directory lists Fire Safety & Prevention at 908-468-1696, while the state directory lists Fire Official John K Daniels at (908) 735-2275 (the construction office line). The email jdaniels@clintonnj.gov comes from the state directory; the Town directory shows only an email link for Jack Daniels.

open_questions: Does the Town still require the portable fire extinguisher at resale after P.L.2025, c.19?
Is the owner self-certification with a notary still accepted for sales, or only for rentals?
How long is the Construction Records Clearance valid if closing is delayed?
